    Resolvable-Error Rank FDR of the Cell Score

    rank_fdr.Rd

    Estimates how reliable the ranking of significant cells is. Calling the top k significant cells by score, a call is false if the cell is below the k-th score by more than the data can resolve: by more than one standard deviation of the estimation noise of its score difference with the cells at the cut-off. Near-ties within that noise are not counted as errors. The estimated FDR at k is the average over the called cells of the probability of such an error when the enrichments are drawn from N(e_hat, Sigma).

    rank_fdr(
  W,
  enrichment,
  Sigma,
  small = rep(FALSE, length(enrichment)),
  alpha = 0.05,
  pct = 1:50,
  n_draws = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  chunk = 100
)

    Arguments

    W

    I x K matrix of cell topic weights, rows summing to one (w_ik proportional to l_ik times the number of peaks in topic k).

    enrichment

    Length-K vector of raw S-LDSC enrichment estimates.

    Sigma

    K x K covariance of enrichment, e.g. the Sigma element of ldsc_jackknife_cov().

    small

    Logical length-K vector, TRUE for topics floored for their annotation size (always contribute e_k = 1).

    alpha

    BH level defining significant cells. Default 0.05.

    pct

    Percentages of significant cells at which to evaluate the FDR. Default 1:50.

    n_draws

    Number of enrichment draws. Default 1000.

    seed

    Optional random seed, for reproducibility.

    chunk

    Draws processed at a time, to bound memory. Default 100.

    Value

    A list with

    • curve: data frame with pct (percentage of significant cells called), k (number called) and fdr (estimated FDR)

    • mean_fdr: mean estimated FDR over the curve (top 1-50% by default)

    • fdr_top10: estimated FDR when calling the top 10% of significant cells

    • n_sig: number of significant cells

    • sig: logical length-I vector marking the significant cells

    With fewer than two significant cells the FDR is undefined: curve is NULL and mean_fdr, fdr_top10 are NA.

    Definitions

    The cell score is c_i = sum_k w_ik e_k, with the same flooring rule as get_cs(): a topic flagged in small, or whose (drawn) enrichment is negative, contributes e_k = 1. Significant cells are those with one-sided BH-adjusted p < alpha for c_i > 1; only they are ranked. The observed order is by the score from enrichment.

    Margin: when the top k are called, called cell i gets m_i = sqrt(mean_j (w_i - w_j)' Sigma_f (w_i - w_j)), the root-mean-square estimation SD of its score difference with the cells j ranked within 1% of the significant cells of position k in the observed order, where Sigma_f is Sigma with the floored topics' rows and columns set to zero. Cells with the same topic mix as the cells at the cut-off have a margin near zero; cells from another part of the topic space have a larger one.

    Estimate: for each draw e* ~ N(e_hat, Sigma), floored per draw, the drawn scores are s* = W e* and s*_(k) is the k-th largest drawn score among the significant cells. A called cell counts as false in the draw if s*_(k) - s*_i > m_i. The FDR at k is the fraction of false calls, averaged over draws.

    Interpretation

    The FDR is the expected share of called cells that are detectably worse than the cut-off. It reflects the GWAS noise in the enrichment estimates; errors in the fitted topic loadings are not modelled. The curve is usually highest for the very top cells, where cells from different topics compete, and falls toward zero as more cells are called, so it is best read at fixed fractions (fdr_top10, or the curve) rather than as a cut-off rule. In simulations (20 settings, about 480 runs) its average over runs agreed with the actual share of resolvable errors within run-to-run noise, and that share tracked how often a run put the wrong cell population on top. A single run whose enrichment estimates confidently favour the wrong topic gets a low FDR; such runs cannot be detected from the run itself.

    See also

    get_cs(), which calls this and returns the result as rank_fdr.
